messages:
mina: Morning — nightly eval spiked on JP polite/honorific outputs for the int8 bring-up. Not a tokenization crash, more like style collapse to casual speech.

akio: Seen the alert. Which model variant? int8/quant config?

mina: redwood-open-3b@v2 + int8-fast quant profile (our new CI job). Batch of 2k JP prompts, polite_accuracy metric dropped from 0.93 -> 0.57 overnight.

denise: ugh. attaching a couple of failing examples below. looks like敬語 (keigo) replaced by casual ~
```
# prompt:
"お客様にご案内させていただきます。以下をご確認ください。"
# expected (polite):
"お客様にはご案内申し上げます。ご確認いただけますでしょうか。"
# actual (int8):
"お客さんに案内するよ。確認してね。"
```

yuki: that example makes it obvious — verb forms got simplified (polite -> plain). could be a head/scale change in the top layers after quantization.

akio: i'd also check whether the detokenizer fallback for small vocab pieces changed. int8 rounding sometimes favors subword merges that prefer colloquial pieces.

denise: i ran a quick token-diff: polite suffixes like "いただけます" tokenized into two pieces in fp16 but into a single low-frequency token in int8 run. frequency shift may bias decoding.

mina: plan: (1) reproduce locally with deterministic seeds, (2) run fp16 vs int8 greedy and beam to compare probs, (3) bisect quant commit window. who can take 1 & 2?

yuki: i'll run local reproducer now. command i'll use: 
```bash
# reproduce polite_accuracy on sample set
python evals/run_promptset.py --model redwood-open-3b --weight-format int8 --prompts data/jp_polite_set.json --seed 42 --output out/int8_run.json
python evals/run_promptset.py --model redwood-open-3b --weight-format fp16 --prompts data/jp_polite_set.json --seed 42 --output out/fp16_run.json
```

akio: i'll check quantization params used in the CI artifact: per-channel vs per-tensor, scale clipping thresholds, and whether we enabled symmetric quant. That often flips small negative logits and changes softmax ordering.

denise: adding the specific metric artifacts to the ticket. eval-bot: posted nightly job diff link: https://ci.redwood.ai/nightly/179999/quant-jp-keigo

eval-bot: nightly job 1799991111: polite_accuracy -36.2% relative, top-1 token drift heatmap attached (see CI page).

mina: if bisect points to quant scaler change, rollback candidate is to revert to per-channel scale and re-run int8 tuning. if it's tokenizer merge, we may need new merge exceptions for keigo morphemes.

yuki: preliminary local outputs: fp16 keeps "いただけます" with prob 0.82, int8 shows 0.18 and picks plain form. will upload diffs.

akio: another quick check — run layernorm fp32 passthrough on top 2 layers in int8 runtime (we have a flag) to see if normalization quantization is the culprit. command: 
```bash
./serve_local --model redwood-open-3b --quant=int8 --ln-passthrough=top2 --port 8080
```

denise: can we also add a small human-eval prompt set for keigo correctness to the nightly so we don't miss this again? current promptset was too general.

mina: agreed. denise please add 50 targeted prompts to data/jp_polite_set.json (include honorific verbs, passive constructions, and customer-facing templates). yuki/akio we'll aim for a bisect result by EOD. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

akio: noted. starting artifact diff now. ping if anyone finds a quick mitigant we can deploy to canary.

yuki: upload done: out/int8_run.json & diffs at s3://redwood-evals/nightlies/1799991111/

mina: thanks — assign ticket RFC-3247, will link CI traces and add rollout pause.

denise: filing the human-eval add now. thanks all. :thumbsup:
